newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey says low inflation vital for housing.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey says low inflation vital for housing.

text.p: Low inflation is vital to foster home ownership and urban redevelopment, Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey said Wednesday, but he said not all politicians seem to share the same feeling.

In remarks prepared for delivery to a community development lending conference sponsored by the Dallas Fed bank, he warned "the political temptation to try to solve economic problems with the printing press" never works as well as keeping inflation in check.
A text of Lindsey's remarks was released in Washington.
"While the commitment of the Federal Reserve to preserving a low-inflation environment is unwavering, I cannot assure you that all politicians feel the same way," Lindsey said.
"Nor can I guarantee you that sustaining the fight against inflation will not mean a temporary rise in interest rates at some time in the future," he added.
He said great progress had been made in making it easier for low and moderate-income people to qualify for mortgages and to own homes.
But he questioned whether the effort has peaked and might be "about to enter another crash in the economic, political and regulatory underpinnings" of redevelopment.

Stressing that low inflation was the key for promoting ownership, Lindsey complained: "Unfortunately, some of those politicians who express the most concern about these issues do not understand this fact."
He also urged public authorities involved in urban redevelopment to seek partners in private markets.
Regulators have gotten banks to cooperate by requiring them to comply with rules on lending to low-income communities and now it is time for authorities to work with the bankers, he said.
